title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes on moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic not 2. On the previous page Grothendieck studies a group D of order 8. It is an extension of W = D_ab (≅ F_2^2, non-canonically) by F_2. W carries a distinguished element ϖ and two further elements c, d, corresponding to sets C and D. He computes Aut D as a semidirect product of ±1 by W.

This page combines that group theory with the combinatorial 'square' Q. Here Q is a carré (4 vertices with an antipodism). The machine transcription's 'corps' and 'quaternions' should read 'carré(s)'.

1. A point suffices to rebuild Q up to unique isomorphism, but only Q 'modulo antipodism'.
2. He takes the standard (épinglé) square Q_0 and its automorphism group D_4 = Aut(Q_0), the dihedral group of order 8. It sits in the canonical exact sequence 1 → F_2 → D_4 → F_2^2 → 1. The F_2 is generated by the antipodism (the central half-turn). The quotient F_2^2 records the action on two 2-element sets: the two diagonals and the two pairs of opposite sides. In his notation these are D and C.
3. Torsor (twisted-form) bookkeeping:
   - A varying D (the data D, C) amounts to a torsor under the quotient F_2^2, i.e. two 2-element sets.
   - A varying square amounts to a torsor under D_4 itself.
   - Equivalently, a varying square is a lifting of the given action into a transitive action on a 4-set S whose quotient by the antipodism, S/±, is identified with D.
   - A dual description exists via C or D^+.
4. Remark: Aut(D_4) ≅ D_4, but not via inner automorphisms (Inn ≅ F_2^2, Out ≅ F_2). He suggests there may be an equivalence of groupoids (squares) ≃ (groups isomorphic to D_4), not given by Q ↦ Aut(Q), which 'deserves to be understood'.
5. The next page settles this. For D ≅ D_4, let S be the four non-central involutions with x' = xa (a the central involution). This gives a square Q_D. The functor D ↦ Q_D is an equivalence of groupoids, with the inverse given by generators and commutator relations.

Verification: Aut(D) acts faithfully on S, since the reflections generate D. Both Aut(D) and Aut(Q_D) have order 8, so Aut(D) → Aut(Q_D) is an isomorphism. Every square is isomorphic to the standard one, so the functor is essentially surjective. Hence it is an equivalence.

Purpose: bookkeeping of level-2 / theta-type (Heisenberg-like, order-8) symmetry data attached to elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2, expressed as twisted forms (torsors) of combinatorial squares.
errors: No mathematical errors. The usage of D vs D^+ vs the set D is notationally overloaded and the lifting statement ('S/± ≃ D') is sketchy, but consistent with the torsor picture.
Q ↦ Aut(Q) is correctly flagged as NOT the equivalence: Aut of a square is D_4, but this assignment does not invert D ↦ Q_D naturally (it does not respect the groupoid structure).

ideas.what: Twisted forms of a square ↔ D_4-torsors; twisted forms of the pair (diagonals, side-pairs) ↔ torsors under the quotient F_2^2
ideas.modern_name: Nonabelian H^1 / descent classification of forms by Aut-torsors
ideas.where_published: SGA 1, SGA 3, Giraud's Cohomologie non abélienne (general principle)

ideas.what: Aut(D_4) ≅ D_4 with outer part F_2
ideas.modern_name: Automorphism group of the dihedral group of order 8

ideas.what: Equivalence of groupoids (groups ≅ D_4) ≃ (combinatorial squares) via the non-central involutions with antipodism x ↦ xa
ideas.modern_name: Natural identification of D_4 with Aut of the square of its reflections (functorial form of Aut(D_8) ≅ D_8)

missed.claim: A clean groupoid-level statement: groups isomorphic to D_4 form a groupoid equivalent to that of combinatorial squares, though not via Q ↦ Aut(Q). This is a small, folklore-level observation, used here for level-2/theta-structure bookkeeping on elliptic curves.
missed.quote: il y a peut-être une équivalence de [carrés] ≈ (groupes isom. à D_4) (mais qui ne donnerait pas Q ↦ Aut(Q) !), qui mériterait d'être comprise
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Marginal. It gives a canonical way to view twisted forms of the order-8 Heisenberg/theta group as twisted squares, but this is easily derivable and implicit in the literature on level-2 structures.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine finite-group and torsor bookkeeping (D_4 = Aut of a square, Aut(D_4) ≅ D_4, forms classified by torsors). It is pleasant, but nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: 'le corps épinglé Q_0' should read 'le carré épinglé Q_0'
'tandis que celle d'un corps variant' should read 'd'un carré variant'
'(ce sont en fait D et C, des cot. adm. ...)' likely refers to the two 2-element sets (diagonals / pairs of opposite sides) named D and C
'(mais pas via automorph. intérieurs, bien sûr)': 'pas' is not struck in the sense intended; it means not via inner automorphisms
'(mais qui ne donnerait pas Q ↦ Aut(Q) !)': 'ne' is inserted and a word above is struck
